title: Conditions for runaway ruptures during reservoir operations: Magnitude–frequency distribution implications and application to Groningen
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a theoretical analysis of an induced seismic rupture propagating from a gas reservoir into the underburden. We use linear elastic fracture mechanics to determine the conditions for self-arrested or runaway ruptures. We derive a phase diagram in which the model parameters (the reservoir thickness, the reservoir pressure depletion, background stress, and fracture energy) are combined into two dimensionless parameters. We apply the analysis to the seismicity induced by gas extraction from the Groningen gas field, where earthquakes have remained confined to the close vicinity of the reservoir. We invert the observations for the model parameters. They indicate subcritical initial stress on the underburden faults, meaning that runaway ruptures are possible in principle, but the conditions required for such events to have happened were most likely not met in reality. The model reproduces the spatial and temporal patterns of observed maximum earthquake magnitudes, and the significant deficit of
                    M
                    > 3.0 events compared to the expectation from the Gutenberg–Richter relationship. This tapering implies that the expected maximum magnitude is nearly insensitive to the total number of induced earthquakes and strongly controlled by the reservoir thickness and pressure depletion. Because the forecast is probabilistic and accounts for uncertainties in the model parameters, it does not exclude runaway ruptures; but such events are found to be unlikely. The model offers an operational framework to forecast earthquake magnitudes by constraining the physical model with measurable parameters.

title: Phase coding supports neuronal replication and enables combinatorial problem solving
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Darwinian neurodynamics posits that the brain searches large solution spaces through iterated cycles of variation and selection on competing neural representations. Testing this hypothesis requires a biologically plausible neural replicator: a mechanism that copies spatiotemporal signals faithfully enough to cumulatively improve good solutions, yet loosely enough to allow exploration. We show that phase-coded spike patterns constitute such a replicator. Spike timing referenced to a local field oscillation is compressed into a transferable spike train and reconstructed by coincidence with the receiver’s own field, without synaptic plasticity or a shared code key. As replication noise rises, the system crosses two thresholds. Below the first, faithful copying sustains patterns as dynamic memory. Between the two thresholds, pattern populations evolve. On two hard combinatorial benchmarks, the traveling salesman problem and NK fitness landscapes, neural replication remains competitive with standard search methods at a matched evaluation budget. Beyond the second, an Eigen-like error threshold, inherited information collapses. The network architecture tunes the exploration-exploitation balance: high-degree lattices, where local competition is stronger, exploit smooth landscapes, while low-degree lattices, where weaker competition preserves diversity, search more broadly on rugged landscapes. The framework predicts phase-locked information transfer and phylogenetic structure in replay, as well as a selective loss of combinatorial problem solving beyond the error threshold. These results indicate that a single neurobiological substrate can support memory, variation, and selection, and point to evolutionary dynamics as a candidate computational principle for cognition.

title: Tumor cell–intrinsic E47 functions as a critical suppressor in antitumor immunity via the FBXL2–PD-L1 axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The transcription factor E47, encoded by the
                    TCF3
                    gene, is essential for B and T cell lineage commitment and development. However, whether tumor cell–intrinsic E47 contributes to tumor immunosurveillance remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that E47 functions as a critical suppressor of antitumor immunity. Clinical analyses reveal that increased intratumoral
                    TCF3
                    expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Silencing of E47 in tumor cells markedly inhibits tumor growth, increases infiltration of cytotoxic CD8
                    +
                    T cells, and decreases PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, E47 transcriptionally represses
                    FBXL2
                    , which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes PD-L1 polyubiquitination at K270 and proteasomal degradation. Restoration of FBXL2 effectively reverses E47-induced PD-L1 upregulation and tumor growth. Strikingly, Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug nebivolol, an activator of FBXL2, significantly enhances antitumor immunity and improves the efficacy of CTLA-4 blockade therapy in syngeneic tumor mouse models. Together, this study uncovers the E47–FBXL2 axis as a critical pathway governing PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for improving the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking—Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.

title: Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
India routinely experiences some of the highest concentrations of fine particulate matter (PM
                    2.5
                    ) air pollution in the world. Although India’s population predominantly lives in rural areas and smaller cities, policy efforts to date have emphasized air pollution in India’s large cities. In contrast, there is limited understanding of air pollutant dynamics in India’s rural and less urbanized areas. Here, we established a well-calibrated lower-cost PM
                    2.5
                    sensor network spanning a wide range of urbanicity (population densities: 300 to 30,000 people/km
                    2
                    ) outside and inside of Delhi. The network of 49 sites incorporated a 160 km measurement transect to capture ambient PM
                    2.5
                    trends of the Delhi megacity, as well as stratified measurements in villages, small cities, and Delhi itself. We report on data from 5 mo of operation (July–November 2024) spanning the cleanest and most polluted times of the year. PM
                    2.5
                    concentrations at rural sites consistently exceeded those at urban sites by about 20% during every month of our study. Analysis of diurnal PM
                    2.5
                    cycles showed sharp morning (approximately 06:00–10:00 LT) and evening (approximately 16:00–20:00 LT) concentration peaks at rural sites that were absent at urban sites. We attribute these events to widespread use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry in suburban and rural settings. These striking enhancements in rural air pollution are missed by satellite remote sensing data, and our findings run contrary to the general societal perception that Indian cities are pollution hotspots relative to rural areas.

title: Topological validation of generated scientific images
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Synthetic data have become an indispensable tool for validation, standards development, and product design across a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines. One of the earliest examples arose in energy systems, where security and confidentiality constraints motivated the development of synthetic power grids and, in turn, novel topological and geometric approaches for evaluating their fidelity. Today, synthetic scientific imagery has emerged as a new critical tool in a variety of applications, ranging from autonomous driving, robotics, and Internet-of-Things technologies to in silico trials, digital twins, and remote sensing of environment. Yet the rigorous assessment of such synthetic images and quantification of their associated uncertainties remains a fundamental challenge. Building on the recent advances in the topological and geometric validation of synthetic power grids, we develop a systematic framework for comparing image data through the persistence of their multiscale shape patterns using the statistical formalism of survival analysis. While the tools of persistent homology and statistical survival analysis are both mature methodologies, they have so far developed largely in isolation. Unlike more traditional comparison methods such as pixel-level similarity or distributional summaries that often fail to capture the complex, multiscale structural characteristics of modern scientific imagery, our approach shows the capability to systematically assess the mismatch between different images at all scales simultaneously, while characterizing the associated uncertainty. The resulting synergistic methodology establishes a broadly applicable statistical topological framework for validating synthetic scientific imagery and, more generally, complex synthetic data products.

title: Humans show limited ability to distinguish human-authored from AI-generated political content on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: This study employs a set of behavioral experiments to examine how individuals perceive the humanness of social media posts about the 2024 U.S. presidential debate between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump. Posts presented in the experiment were authored either by humans or chatbots, varying the large language model (LLM), the model architecture, the social media platform, and the political personas. Participants judged randomly paired posts to identify which they perceived to be AI-generated. We find that human-authored posts were on average perceived as more human-like than AI outputs generated from five of the six LLMs in this study. However, participants’ ability to detect AI-generated content is limited. They do so only slightly above chance in human–AI pairs, and this ability weakens for newer LLMs, varies by platform, and reflects partisan bias. Only posts generated with Llama 3.3 scored, on average, higher on perceived humanness than human-authored posts. The social media platform also mattered, with participants distinguishing human from AI on most platforms (YouTube, TikTok, Truth Social), but not on X/Twitter. Incivility and negative emotions are associated with high humanness perceptions, and partisan identity also shaped evaluations, with Republican respondents more likely to view ideologically misaligned AI posts as AI-generated.

title: Structural and biochemical impact of clinically relevant constitutively active parathyroid hormone receptor 1 mutations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Parathyroid hormone receptor 1 (PTH1R) constitutively active mutants, including H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P, are responsible for Jansen’s metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, a form of short-limbed dwarfism. Here, we expand pharmacological understanding and present cryoelectron microscopy structures of the constitutively active PTH1R mutants, H223
                    2.50
                    K, H223
                    2.50
                    R, and T410
                    6.42
                    P, in complex with Gs protein and PTH(1–34), and H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P in the ligand free Gs complexed form. These reveal modifications in polar networks that allow for constitutive G protein coupling and subsequent signaling. In the absence of a peptide bound to the extracellular side of the PTH1R, TM6 adopts a distinct conformation relative to the PTH(1–34) bound wild-type PTH1R coupled with Gs. Combined with molecular dynamics analysis of inactive and Gs bound receptors, this work reveals distinct mechanisms that lead to differing receptor activation states and consequently promote distinct constitutive activity and agonist-mediated pharmacological profiles.

title: Unsupervised Bayesian neural networks enable inference of complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Birth–death models quantify macroevolutionary and epidemiological processes, including speciation, extinction, and transmission, based on phylogenetic trees. Extensions of these models incorporate external covariates as predictors of these parameters, for instance linking traits or environmental variables with changes in these rates. However, the dependencies between predictors and model parameters are typically restricted to linear, additive effects and may thus fail to capture complex, nonlinear relationships underlying evolutionary dynamics. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that leverages unsupervised Bayesian neural networks to flexibly model functional relationships between these parameters and a broad set of predictors, including categorical traits, quantitative variables, and time series data. Based on these covariates, the network weights and thus the resulting birth–death dynamics are estimated jointly with the phylogenetic tree, obtained directly from sequence alignment data. Extensive simulations show that this approach accurately recovers predictor–parameter relationships, mitigates overfitting, and remains robust across both macroevolutionary and epidemiological contexts. Using explainable AI, we further show that our framework reliably identifies the most influential predictors and yields interpretable descriptions of their impact on the inferred rates. Finally, we apply our method in two empirical analyses: linking SARS-CoV-2 migration dynamics with travel data during its early spread in Europe, and inferring trait- and time-dependent speciation and extinction rates in the diversification of platyrrhines. Our framework substantially expands the capabilities of birth–death models, providing a powerful and flexible approach to infer complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes.

title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell–tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.

title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

title: Isotope evidence for changing methane sources at high northern latitudes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The renewed increase of methane (CH
                    4
                    ) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition (
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    ) in the 21st century indicates a fundamental shift in the global CH
                    4
                    cycle. Here, we investigate the origin of this
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    trend by determining isotope source signatures of CH
                    4
                    emissions based on high and mid-northern latitude observations. A clear latitude gradient and seasonal cycle of the source signatures reflect the spatially and temporally varying contributions of the different sources, each with distinct signatures. We find a large shift in the source signature after 2007 between −3.6 and −5.1‰ at high northern latitudes, and a moderate change between −0.4 and −0.9‰ at mid-northern latitudes. The decrease in
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    source signature is likely caused by a shift from thermogenic and pyrogenic to microbial sources, accompanied by a likely decrease in the isotopic signature of the microbial emissions, possibly resulting from climate change. Our results suggest that current inverse models may underestimate the shift between fossil and microbial emissions at high northern latitudes, or that microbial methanogenesis pathways change much more strongly than currently believed. Source changes at high latitudes have a disproportionate contribution to the observed trend in atmospheric
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    .

title: Human retinal capillary network analysis using vascular interconnectivity optical coherence tomography angiography
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The human retina is perfused by capillary plexuses at distinct inner-retinal depths. Interconnections among these plexuses are critical for perfusion, but are difficult to quantify using 2D en face optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Diabetic retinopathy (DR) involves extensive microvascular remodeling, however the topological changes, especially at the interplexus level, are challenging to assess in vivo. We introduce Network Analysis using Vascular Interconnectivity (NAVI) OCTA, a framework that reconstructs the 3D retinal capillary network across the superficial vascular (SVP), intermediate capillary (ICP), and deep capillary (DCP) plexuses. The reconstructed macula-wide vasculature contains more than 10,000 vessel segments, and can be quantitatively analyzed using network representation. This method reveals a divergent alteration in interplexus connectivity in early DR: superficial-to-intermediate connections decrease, while intermediate-to-deep connections increase. This finding is consistent with previous histological studies, but is quantitatively measured in vivo in the human retina, opening the possibility for longitudinal studies of capillary remodeling. In addition to size-based metrics (e.g., vessel length or area), NAVI can quantify recurrent small-scale connectivity patterns (motifs). Finally, joint connectivity-hemodynamics analysis is demonstrated in eyes with DR, where capillary topology and flow speed can be quantified using a single OCTA acquisition. NAVI OCTA is a scalable, computational framework that supports analysis of retinal vasculature as a network and provides an in vivo approach to study capillary remodeling in early DR.

title: Wnts are endothelial cell–derived PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Wingless/Int-1 (Wnts) are secreted glycoproteins and canonical Frizzled receptor ligands. Recent evidence indicates that some Wnts can also bind to polycystin 1 (PKD1), a large transmembrane protein which can couple to polycystin 2 (PKD2) to form a nonselective cation channel. The functional significance of PKD1, PKD2, and Wnt-mediated PKD1 signaling in native cell types is poorly understood. Here, we tested the hypothesis that Wnts regulate arterial contractility, investigated the signaling mechanisms and cell types involved, and examined the cellular source of vasoactive Wnts. Our data show that Wnt9b and Wnt5a are endothelial cell (EC)-dependent vasodilators. Wnt9b stimulates vasodilation via EC PKD1/PKD2, whereas Wnt5a acts via both EC PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors. Wnts stimulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase and small conductance Ca
                    2+
                    -activated K
                    +
                    channels in ECs to produce vasodilation. Wnt9b and Wnt5a are present in plasma and intravenous infusion of Wnt9b stimulates an EC PKD1-dependent reduction in systemic blood pressure. Intravascular flow activates angiotensin II type 1 receptors which, through G
                    q/11
                    and Porcupine signaling, stimulate ECs to secrete Wnt9b and Wnt5a. Wnts which are secreted by ECs in response to flow activate PKD1/PKD2 on ECs and this mechanism contributes to the flow-mediated vasodilation. In summary, we show that Wnts are autocrine/paracrine vasodilator proteins. Intravascular flow stimulates ECs to secrete Wnts, which then act via PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors on ECs to induce vasodilation.

title: Rethinking broad diet breadth as a sign of scarcity: A 50,000-y record of subsistence from northwestern Australia
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The prey choice model, widely applied in archaeological reconstructions of Pleistocene diet, predicts that people will initially focus on a narrow suite of high-ranked prey before broadening their diet to include lower-ranked species as necessitated by subsistence needs. However, evidence from arid and semiarid northern Australia challenges this assumption. Archaeological faunal records demonstrate that a broad diet was established early and persisted through the Holocene. We argue that these diverse diets do not indicate resource scarcity, but rather represent an ideal strategy for exploiting abundant, low-risk hidden, or cryptic prey, as well as high-risk, conspicuous prey within an environment characterized by unpredictable rainfall. This pattern also necessitates reconceptualizing traditional notions of prey rank and dietary breadth. Rather than adhering to static prey rankings, northern Australian peoples skillfully adapted their hunting strategies in response to fluctuating nutritional content and pursuit costs of different species. The most successful subsistence strategy in this region was therefore one of high responsiveness and flexibility, manifesting as a consistently broad diet. This case study suggests that the relationship between human dietary breadth and resource abundance is more nuanced in situations of abundant, cryptic prey.

title: NSP1–SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in
                    
                      Stat1
                      −/−
                    
                    pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1–SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1–SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in
                    
                      Samd9l
                      −/−
                    
                    mice. Combined deletion of
                    Samd9l
                    and
                    Stat1
                    permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.

title: Influence of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The effect of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories is investigated. To this end, we first show the equivalence between noninertial effects and a completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) map. In this formulation, the Unruh effect is equivalent to a bosonic amplifier channel. The effect of this map on a generic quantum resource is investigated by studying the role of the CPTP map on the three core ingredients of a resource theory, namely, the free states, the free operations, and the resource quantifiers. We show several general statements can be made about these three components of a resource theory in the presence of noninertial motion.

title: A chromatin biology assessment of AlphaFold3
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold have achieved remarkable success in predicting structures of single proteins and multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold3 now incorporates the capability to model complexes containing nucleic acids and chemically modified side chains. Investigators can now predict structures of proteins bound to chromatin, where interactions with nucleosomal DNA and histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) converge to control genome function. To evaluate its robustness in modeling chromatin complexes, we benchmarked AlphaFold3 on 115 structures containing nucleosomes whose coordinates were released by the Protein Data Bank after the training set cutoff date. We find that AlphaFold3 excels at predicting interactions with the histone octamer core and with PTMs. By contrast, AlphaFold3 struggles to predict structures of chromatin factors that primarily engage nucleosomal DNA, notably transcription factors and chromatin remodelers. We also show that AlphaFold3 can faithfully recapitulate known PTM recognition patterns, matching experimentally determined specificity profiles. This assessment of the capabilities and limitations of AlphaFold3 in chromatin structural biology provides a roadmap for its effective application to studies of chromatin regulation and PTM readout, while identifying key areas for future refinement of algorithms for predicting interactions between proteins and nucleic acids.

title: Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex inhibition has potential for shortening leishmaniasis treatment duration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Leishmaniasis affects approximately 1 million people annually with visceral infections resulting in death if left untreated and the cutaneous disease leading to disfiguring skin lesions. Leishmaniasis is caused by the
                    Leishmania
                    spp. parasites and is difficult to treat as existing drugs are far from optimal. Despite increased efforts to identify better drugs for leishmaniasis, there are few new chemical entities that have entered clinical development, thus highlighting the persistent need for such compounds. Here we describe GNF5885, an orally available and parasite-selective inhibitor of
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex. GNF5885 was derived through phenotypic optimization of buparvaquone. GNF5885 exhibits unparalleled efficacy in vivo and can efficiently clear parasites from mice in models of visceral and cutaneous infections. Furthermore, its ability to clear parasites rapidly with short treatment regimens makes it particularly desirable for treating patients residing in regions endemic to leishmaniasis. Cryo-EM structure of the
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex with GNF5885 at 2.8 Å resolution revealed that the inhibitor binds in the Qi ubiquinone-binding pocket. Our data provide validation of the
                    Leishmania
                    cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of leishmaniasis and underscore the possibility of developing a short-course oral treatment for this neglected disease. In addition, the availability of the cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex costructure with GNF5885 opens an opportunity to rationally design new cytochrome
                    bc1
                    complex inhibitors suitable for clinical development.

title: Topology‐Encoded Polymer Networks for Thermo‐Responsive Wrinkling With Dynamic Diffraction Tunability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Thermo‐responsive wrinkles provide a scalable route to adaptive optical surfaces. However, achieving thermally tunable structural color with high diffraction efficiency remains challenging, limiting their applications in optical devices and information encryption. This challenge arises from conventional wrinkle systems relying on empirical macroscopic parameters and lacking molecular‐level design principles based on network topology. Herein, we propose a crosslinker chain‐length programming strategy to construct thermally responsive optical wrinkled surfaces with encoded polymer network topology. By tuning bismaleimide crosslinker chain length, network topology and thermomechanical response are regulated, directing thermally induced surface instability into oriented periodic wrinkles with programmable structural color and diffraction efficiency. Using crosslinker chain length and prestrain as design variables, a two‐dimensional diffraction efficiency design map is constructed to delineate diffractive and non‐diffractive regimes, achieving a maximum diffraction efficiency of 22.7%. Chain length‐dependent UV‐induced maleimide dimerization enables spatially resolved orthogonal patterning, allowing hidden information to be written and read out optically under manual stretching without external devices. Dynamic Diels–Alder (D–A) reversibility supports partial wrinkle amplitude erasure, enabling post‐read information invalidation. This study bridges molecularly encoded polymer network topology and macroscopic optical performance, providing molecular‐level design principles for multistimuli‐responsive optical platforms and advanced anti‐counterfeiting materials.

title: Nonclassical Electrostriction: The Insights From X‐Ray Absorption Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nonclassical electrostriction (NCES) has emerged in a growing class of ionic solids that exhibit electromechanical responses far exceeding predictions of the conventional Newnham scaling law despite moderate dielectric permittivity and high elastic modulus. Unlike classical electrostriction, which is associated with nearly uniform anharmonic deformation of the crystal lattice, NCES originates from the field‐induced reorganization of a small population of locally distorted structural units. This Review examines the unique role of x‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy in identifying the electromechanically active structural units, resulting in the understanding of atomistic mechanisms underlying this behavior. Element‐specific x‐ray absorption near edge structure and extended XAFS (EXAFS) measurements identify local symmetry breaking, defect‐associated elastic dipoles, multimodal bond‐length distributions, and strongly anharmonic bonds that remain “hidden” from average‐structure probes. Field‐modulated, high energy resolution, and differential XAFS further isolate the minority structural units directly responsible for macroscopic strain. Aliovalent and isovalent dopants are shown to produce distinct microscopic mechanisms, involving vacancy‐associated static and dynamic elastic dipoles, respectively, embedding strong attributes of anharmonicity. These results establish local structure and bond dynamics as key descriptors of NCES and highlight in situ, stimulus‐modulated XAFS as a powerful route for uncovering and ultimately controlling electromechanical coupling in defect‐engineered materials.

title: Learning to Program Dimple‐Encoded Strips for Morphing Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Programmable morphing structures that translate local mechanical states into global shape transformations enable deployable, adaptive, and reconfigurable systems. Dimple‐encoded elastic strips provide a minimal platform in which arrays of bistable dimples can collectively program large bending deformation. Yet the nonlinear mapping from the encoded geometry to the final configuration makes inverse design challenging. Here, we report a learning‐enabled strategy for programming dimple‐encoded strips with prescribed morphing profiles and using them as building blocks for higher‐level morphing architectures. Finite‐element simulations are converted into centerline‐based tangent‐field representations to train a one‐dimensional convolutional neural‐network surrogate that maps local dimple encoding and strip geometry to global shape. The trained surrogate enables gradient‐based inverse design of target morphologies, with optimized designs validated by independent simulations and physical prototypes. Variable‐width strip modules expand the accessible shape space and enable width‐conditioned curvature programming. Rotational tessellation of programmed strip modules creates dome‐like morphing shells, while hierarchical integration of curvature‐programmed strips with folding modules yields an artifical flower exhibiting sequential opening through dimple switching. These results establish dimple‐encoded strips as learnable building blocks that connect local bistable encoding, inverse design, and hierarchical shape formation, providing a route toward task‐specific morphing components for soft robotics, adaptive interfaces, and deployable structures.

title: Self‐Assembled Nanoplatform for Modulating the ATP‐Adenosine Pathway and CD8+ T Cell Metabolism to Potentiate Radiotherapy‐Mediated Antitumor Immunity
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Radiotherapy (RT) is one of the primary clinical modalities for tumor treatment, yet its therapeutic efficacy is restricted by post‐RT immunosuppression and impaired function of tumor‐infiltrating cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Herein, we fabricate self‐assembled nanoparticles based on sodium metatungstate (POM1) and spermidine (Spd), followed by polyethylene glycol (PEG) modification to enhance biocompatibility (denoted as POM1‐Spd/PEG). Structural characterization and molecular simulations confirm that the core POM1‐Spd complex is assembled via electrostatic and van der Waals interactions, with each POM1 cluster stably anchoring two Spd molecules to form a dimeric supramolecular architecture. Benefiting from these weak intermolecular interactions, POM1‐Spd/PEG can efficiently disassemble in the weakly acidic tumor microenvironment to release free POM1 and Spd. Notably, we uncover that POM1 possesses unrecognized dual functional properties, which act as both a potent radiosensitizer to amplify RT‐induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and an efficient CD39 inhibitor that prevents the conversion of ICD‐released ATP to immunosuppressive adenosine (ADO), thereby reversing ADO‐mediated tumor immunosuppression and sustaining robust antitumor immune activation. Furthermore, the released Spd upregulates fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis in CD8
                    +
                    T cells, consequently boosting their proliferation and cytotoxic effector functions. When combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, this strategy can effectively trigger systemic antitumor immunity to further enhance therapeutic efficacy and suppress the growth and metastasis of distant tumors. Collectively, our work develops a distinctive self‐assembled nanoplatform capable of achieving radiosensitization, regulating the ATP‐ADO pathway, and improving CD8
                    +
                    T cell metabolism, offering a promising approach to amplify RT efficacy by remodeling antitumor immunity.

title: Bioinspired Membrane Fusion–Gated Hydrogel Biosensor for Extraction‐Free Viral RNA Detection of Infectious Influenza Virus
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Emerging infectious diseases driven by zoonotic spillover demand rapid and reliable molecular diagnostics for pathogen identification and surveillance. However, conventional nucleic acid diagnostics cannot distinguish infectious virions from nonviable RNA fragments, limiting infectivity‐resolved virus identification. Here, we report a bioinspired membrane‐coated hydrogel (Memgel) sensor that enables extraction‐free molecular detection of influenza virus while distinguishing fusion‐competent virions from noninfectious viral material. The platform integrates a cell‐mimetic supported lipid bilayer with a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel matrix encapsulating recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) reagents. Under endosome‐mimicking acidic conditions, hemagglutinin‐mediated membrane fusion selectively delivers viral genomic RNA from infectious virions into the hydrogel matrix, triggering sequence‐specific amplification while suppressing signals from free viral RNA fragments. As a proof of concept, the Memgel sensor was evaluated for the detection of influenza A (H9N2) in simulated nasal fluid and raw milk matrices, achieving a limit of detection of 10
                    1.23
                    TCID
                    50
                    mL
                    −
                    1
                    while maintaining robust detection performance without RNA extraction. Coupled with a portable fluorescence reader, the system demonstrates compatibility with compact fluorescence‐based readout for future point‐of‐care implementation. This fusion‐gated sensing strategy provides a materials‐based framework for infectivity‐resolved molecular diagnostics of emerging viral pathogens.

title: Metal‐Chelating Molecule‐Enabled Multidentate Molecular Bridge Engineering of the Buried Interface for High‐Performance Fully Printed Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Modules
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Carbon‐based perovskite solar modules (C‐PSMs) provide a scalable and metal‐electrode‐free platform for stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet their efficiencies remain constrained by defective and mechanically fragile buried SnO
                    2
                    /perovskite interfaces. Conventional interfacial modifiers generally rely on limited coordination, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve robust passivation and strong interfacial adhesion. Here, we introduce two metal‐chelating molecules to construct multidentate molecular bridges at the buried interface in C‐PSMs. Diglycine disodium (DDS), although capable of coordinating with both SnO
                    2
                    and perovskite, exhibits weak configurational selectivity because multiple interfacial coordination modes are energetically accessible, preventing stable bilateral bridge formation. In contrast, tetrasodium iminodisuccinate (IDS) coordinates with both SnO
                    2
                    and perovskite, constructing a robust bilateral molecular bridge, suppressing interfacial defects, enhancing charge transfer, and interfacial adhesion. Consequently, the fully printed 30 × 30 cm
                    2
                    IDS C‐PSMs achieve a record efficiency of 19.26% with an active area of 563.78 cm
                    2
                    (certified 18.04%, with a mask‐defined area of 487.6 cm
                    2
                    ), which represents the highest reported PCE for a device of this size and architecture. The unencapsulated IDS C‐PSM retains over 90% of its initial efficiency after 1130 h of maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C and over 85% after 2184 h under damp‐heat conditions (85°C and 85% RH).

title: Enhanced Molecular‐Structure Dual‐Recognition by Enzyme‐Embedded Metal‐Phenolic Networks for Wearable Plant Sensing of Pesticides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    On‐site monitoring of plant health using enzyme‐based wearable sensors is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet inherent enzyme instability and poor molecular recognition remain major obstacles. Here, we present a robust plant‐wearable hydrogel sensor based on an acetylcholinesterase‐embedded metal‐phenolic network (AChE@MPN) to overcome these limitations through a dual‐recognition strategy, markedly improving stability and selectivity relative to conventional sensors. The MPN protects the enzyme's native conformation, maintaining catalytic kinetics comparable to those of the free enzyme. Within this architecture, the dual‐recognition strategy integrates metal‐assisted adsorption with enzymatic recognition, engaging pesticide molecules through synergistic P‐O‐Zr coordination, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to yield a 1.41‐fold higher response to phoxim than that obtained with free AChE. Notably, the AChE@MPN exhibits an approximately 88‐fold higher binding affinity for phoxim than for its nonaromatic analog malathion, indicating that the signal gain originates from selective enrichment. These features enable the sensor to discriminate phoxim from interfering substances, with a limit of detection of 2 ng mL
                    −1
                    , and to perform on‐site monitoring of phoxim degradation on living tomato plants. This dual‐recognition design offers a general strategy for pesticide monitoring and may inspire plant‐sensing innovations for sustainable agriculture.

title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Adsorbate‐induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd–Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen‐induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large‐scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H‐driven reconstruction. On Pd‐covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd–Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd–H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen‐induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD‐derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active‐site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet‐dependent, large‐scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Despite the long‐recognized structural diversity and accessibility of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols as synthetic building blocks, their deoxygenative radical difunctionalization remains a formidable challenge due to the lack of a linkage strategy integrating the respective functionalization of non‐adjacent hydroxyl and alkene/alkyne groups. Herein, we present an efficient platform for the deoxygenative radical 1,4‐difunctionalization of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols through an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer‐triggered radical‐relay deoxygenation process. Utilizing 1,3‐benzodithiolylium as an effective hydroxyl‐activating reagent, copper‐catalyzed enantioconvergent 1,4‐perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4‐cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been achieved with excellent regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: Fast‐Discharge‐Induced Non‐Equilibrium Phase Transition in Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathode at High Voltage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The rapid adoption of electric vehicles necessitates lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) that can sustain extreme fast charging (XFC) without rapid degradation. Ni‐rich layered cathodes deliver high energy density, yet their poor stability under high‐rate operation limits practical deployment and the mechanistic origin of fast capacity decay remains poorly understood. Here, using high time‐resolved
                    operando
                    XRD, together with theoretical analyses, we reveal that a rate‐dependent non‐equilibrium H3→H2 phase transition under rapid discharge (≥4 C) induces huge lattice displacement and nanoscale strain, which significantly lower the migration barrier for Ni, thereby promoting irreversible rock‐salt phase formation and structural collapse. Importantly, guided by this mechanistic understanding, we propose a cycling protocol introducing a brief low‐rate discharge step at high voltage (4.5 V→4.0 V), which effectively suppresses the detrimental H2+H3 phase separation and generation of internal stress. Compared to that of the cell under constant high cycling rates (6 C), the capacity retention improves 29% for the one with optimized discharge procedure after 1000 cycles. These results clarify the underneath electrochemical–mechanical degradation behavior of Ni‐rich layered cathodes at different rates (1/3 C, 1 C, 4 C, and 6 C), providing practical guidance for designing durable batteries with superior fast‐charging abilities.

title: Heteroatom‐Modulated Aggregation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Derivatives by Single‐Atom Substitution to Construct NIR‐II‐Absorbing Photothermal Agents With Over 90% Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic small‐molecule photothermal materials with second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) absorption have attracted enormous interest for biomedical applications, yet simultaneously achieving strong NIR‐II absorption and high photothermal conversion efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report to conduct the heteroatom‐modulated aggregation of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives (named as DAQ‐T and DAQ‐Fu) by single‐atom substitution to construct high‐performance NIR‐II‐absorbing photothermal agents. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen‐for‐sulfur substitution precisely modulates electrostatic potential distributions and tailors intermolecular π–π interactions by leveraging the distinct electronegativities of chalcogens, driving a transformation from
                    H
                    ‐aggregation in DAQ‐T to
                    J
                    ‐aggregation in DAQ‐Fu. The resulting
                    J
                    ‐aggregated DAQ‐Fu nanoparticles feature a distinct absorption band at 1064 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 3.26 × 10
                    4
                    L mol
                    −1
                    cm
                    −1
                    , and exhibit an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.4%. This photothermal effect exerts potent antitumor efficacy by regulating apoptosis and immune‐related signaling pathways, enabling the synergy of photothermal therapy and as‐induced immunogenic cell death to suppress both primary and distant tumors growth with about 90% and 63% inhibition rates, respectively, under biocompatible irradiation. This work demonstrates atom‐precise aggregation modulation, offering a promising pathway to engineer NIR‐II‐absorbing organic small‐molecule photothermal agents for synergistic photothermal cancer immunotherapy.

title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled‐Cluster Accurate Free‐Energy Simulations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The mechanism of Brønsted acid‐catalyzed transformations in zeolites is generally described in terms of carbocationic intermediates, yet their thermodynamic stability and mechanistic role remain controversial. Resolving this issue requires chemically accurate free‐energy simulations, which are beyond the reach of conventional density functional theory (DFT) and prohibitively expensive at the coupled‐cluster level. Here, we combine a cluster‐based QM/QM ‐learning strategy with a machine‐learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with near‐CCSD(T) accuracy. Applied to the skeletal isomerization of
                    n
                    ‐butene in chabazite, the resulting free‐energy surfaces (FESs) reveal a mechanistic picture that differs qualitatively from that predicted by generalized‐gradient approximation (GGA) functionals. Rather than proceeding through persistent carbocationic intermediates, the reaction is governed by a cascade of highly transient ionic configurations, while protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) is identified as a short‐lived reactive configuration rather than a genuine metastable intermediate. These findings provide a more physically consistent description of one of the prototypical reactions in zeolite catalysis. More generally, the methodology introduced here provides a practical route toward chemically accurate free‐energy simulations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions involving highly reactive charged species, opening the way to quantitative mechanistic studies of complex catalytic processes.

title: The Self‐Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na+/Ca2+
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge‐like pore structure, a narrow pore‐size distribution, and a high
                    β
                    ‐phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca
                    2+
                    rejection and a Na
                    +
                    /Ca
                    2+
                    separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Solvation‐Directed Electric Double Layer Formation in Low‐Concentration Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The electric double layer (EDL) governs interfacial stability in lithium metal batteries, yet its rational design remains constrained by concentrated electrolytes or complex solvent systems. Here we demonstrate that the EDL in low‐concentration electrolytes (LCEs) can be rationally programmed through anion selection based on their solvation behavior, decoupling interfacial stability from the heavy consumption of lithium salts and sophisticated solvent blends. By systematically screening anions with distinct Li
                    +
                    ‐anion coordination strengths and steric profiles, we formulate a mixed‐anion LCE and uncover a fundamental principle: large, weakly coordinatinganions (WCAs) accumulate at the interface to form a persistent charge‐shielding layer, whereas small, strongly coordinating anions (SCAs) are dynamically driven deeper into the Helmholtz region under polarization, where they actively modulate interfacial (de)solvation kinetics. This solvation‐defined division of labor creates a rationally designed, self‐adaptive EDL that couples electrostatic stabilization with interfacial chemistry. Beyond offering a high‐performance LCE formulation, this work establishes a direct and mechanistic linkage between bulk solvation architecture and interfacial EDL organization in dilute electrolytes, revealing that the EDL can itself be programmed through anion‐specific solvation motifs to dictate interfacial stability, introducing a design paradigm for materially efficient electrolyte engineering based on solvation‐directed EDL formation.

title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Simultaneous CO
                    2
                    conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO
                    2
                    batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO
                    2
                    redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO
                    2
                    reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO
                    2
                    batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO
                    2
                    adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO
                    2
                    antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

title: Manganese‐Catalyzed Electrochemical Nitrogenative‐Oxygenative Cleavage of Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Herein, we report a manganese‐catalyzed electrochemical nitrogenative‐oxygenative scission of olefins to nitriles and carbonyls. Mechanistic and kinetic studies reveal distinct precatalyst‐activation and productive‐turnover regimes, and support conversion of the manganese precursor into a mixed‐valent oxo‐bridged dimanganese(III/IV) species, followed by azide‐dependent formation of a product‐forming manganese species. Notably, polyunsaturated substrates can undergo alkene‐chemoselective cleavage with preferential reaction at the more substituted C═C bond, while the present protocol enables unprecedented reactivity towards activated and unactivated alkenes with broad functional‐group tolerance.

title: Electric‐Field‐Manipulated Reaction Pathway Engineering in Lupinus micranthus‐Like High‐Entropy Alloy Nanowires for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation in direct fuel cells is constrained by CO poisoning and insufficient hydroxyl generation at low potentials. Here we show that anisotropic PtFeCoIrRhCu high‐entropy alloy nanowires with
                    Lupinus micranthus
                    ‐like morphology generate a local electric field through coupling of strain‐induced lattice distortion with charge redistribution, enabling a directional capture‐migration‐dissociation relay of interfacial water for efficient low‐potential hydroxyl generation, in which H
                    2
                    O is preferentially captured at Fe/Co sites, migrates under field polarization, and dissociates at Rh/Ir sites. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals that the electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a more ordered hydrogen‐bond network, facilitating water activation. Density functional theory calculations, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further demonstrate that the generated hydroxyl species accelerate CO oxidative removal and promote the non‐CO oxidation pathway. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a methanol oxidation mass activity of 3.76 A mg
                    Pt
                    −1
                    , 8.36 times that of Pt/C, together with a direct methanol fuel cell peak power density of 163.06 mW cm
                    −2
                    and stable membrane‐electrode operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    . These findings establish strain–charge coupling as a general strategy for engineering interfacial water activation and directing reaction‐pathway selectivity in multimetallic electrocatalysts.
